install_recipe: cd <checkout> && pip install -e '.[dev]' (dev extra: argcomplete, attrs, hypothesis, mock, requests, setuptools, xmlschema). Resolved at verify time: pluggy 1.6.0, iniconfig 2.3.0, packaging 26.3, pygments 2.21.0, hypothesis 6.168.0.
issue_paraphrase: Passing a single comma-terminated argument name to parametrize — for example 'arg,' — together with a list of one-element tuples as the values does not unpack those tuples the way the tuple form ('arg',) does. Each test invocation receives the whole one-element tuple as its argument instead of the single element, so a test expecting the string value fails with something like 'assert ('b',) in ('a', 'b')'. The comma-terminated string form should behave exactly like the equivalent tuple form.
fix_summary: ParameterSet._for_parametrize now detects a trailing comma in the string argnames and sets force_tuple=False for single-argument string form, so comma-terminated 'arg,' behaves like ('arg',) (values are NOT wrapped; the list items are treated as tuples to unpack).
notes: No network needed at test time. Whole verification (both directions + golden tests) takes under ~1 minute at 1 CPU. The unit golden test uses the private Metafunc helper and the functional one uses pytester; both run directly under `python -m pytest` from the repo root. pyproject.toml is the configfile and adds no restrictive addopts.

install_recipe: cd <checkout> && pip install -e '.[dev]' (dev extra: argcomplete, attrs, hypothesis, mock, requests, setuptools, xmlschema). Resolved at verify time: pluggy 1.6.0, iniconfig 2.3.0, packaging 26.3, pygments 2.21.0, hypothesis 6.168.0.
issue_paraphrase: When comparing datetime/timedelta values with pytest.approx using a relative tolerance expressed as a plain number (for example rel=0.01), a TypeError is raised saying the relative tolerance must itself be a timedelta, so percentage-style relative tolerances cannot be used at all for datetime/timedelta comparisons even though plain numbers work for every other value type. Invalid tolerances such as a negative relative tolerance or NaN are also not rejected cleanly and instead surface as confusing errors, like the comparison machinery trying to compare a timedelta with a float.
fix_summary: ApproxTimedelta now accepts rel as a plain number (int/float), validates it (reject negative and NaN rel, reject negative timedelta abs with clear ValueError messages), and computes the effective tolerance as rel * abs(expected) as a timedelta, taking max(abs, rel_tolerance) when both are given. ApproxBase._approx_scalar also routes datetime/timedelta scalars inside sequences/mappings to ApproxTimedelta so rel works there too. Old behavior required rel itself to be a timedelta and used max(abs, rel) directly.
notes: No network needed at test time. Verification of both directions plus the 7 golden tests takes under a minute at 1 CPU. Note the semantics change: rel=timedelta(...) is no longer accepted (must be a number), so older tests that passed rel=timedelta are updated in the fix; a task author must keep the golden test file from the fix commit.

issue_paraphrase: If a monkeypatch mutation fails — for instance setitem or delitem on an immutable mapping proxy, or delattr of an attribute that cannot be deleted (such as a slot attribute on a class) — pytest still records an undo entry for the operation that never happened. Calling undo() afterwards then re-raises the original error (TypeError or AttributeError) instead of being a harmless no-op, and the rollback bookkeeping no longer reflects what was actually changed. Failed mutations should register nothing to undo.
fix_summary: MonkeyPatch.delattr, setitem and delitem now capture the old value first and append the undo entry to self._setattr / self._setitem only after the mutation itself (delattr / dict-style assignment / del) succeeded, so a failed mutation leaves no stale undo record and undo() is a no-op.
notes: No network needed at test time. Verification of both directions plus the four golden tests takes under a minute at 1 CPU. test_setitem_delitem_oldval_captured_before_mutation depends on the make_mapping fixture defined in testing/conftest.py, so run golden tests from the repo root. All four golden tests are plain functions in testing/test_monkeypatch.py.
